newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Jochimsen - dispute with Bonn not yet solved.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Jochimsen - dispute with Bonn not yet solved.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Friday the dispute between the central bank and Bonn over revaluation of reserves had not been resolved yet, and the two sides had merely agreed to find an agreement.
Jochimsen told a news conference the Bundesbank council would discuss the outcome of talks between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer at its meeting next week.
Earlier this week Waigel and Tietmeyer said they had come closer to an agreement.
"As I understand it one has agreed to find an agreement," Jochimsen, also the president of the state central bank in North Rhine-Westphalia, told a news conference.

He welcomed the fact the two sides were on the way to resolving their dispute and said the key issue was that Waigel had dropped his demand for an interim balance sheet and payout of Bundesbank profits in 1997.
Jochimsen also noted the European Monetary Institute had stated that unrealised profits from revaluations must not be paid out to governments.

He saw scope for a payout from a central bank's currency reserves but said there was no scope for a payout from a revaluation of its gold reserves unless gold was sold -- a step the government and the Bundesbank have ruled out.

Jochimsen also said he was "very irritated" at a reported move by the European parliament to push through amendments to the stability and growth pact designed to ensure lasting fiscal discipline after monetary union begins.
"That could also cause a lot of problems for the German government which has placed emphasis on the need for automatic sanctions," Jochimsen said.
